result.rationale: In googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts the diff replaces `const key = googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` with `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema)`. The new helper (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts) returns the full safeParse wrapper (`return refreshTokenResponse;`), not `.data`, so `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })` persists `{ success: true, data: {...} }` as the credential key instead of the credential object itself, corrupting the credential on every refresh.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the refreshed credential is now computed as `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` and then persisted via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. However `parseRefreshTokenResponse` (new file `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`) returns the Zod `safeParse` result object (`{ success, data, error? }`), not `result.data`. Persisting this wrapper into `Credential.key` would change the stored shape and likely break downstream code expecting the raw credential payload. This matches the finding that credentials would be corrupted on refresh.
